  const b=document.getElementById("newgraph"); if(b){ b.textContent="New"; b.style.background=""; b.style.color=""; } }

rebuild_jump.name: rebuildJump()
rebuild_jump.desc: `rebuildJump()` rebuilds the jump-to-node dropdown from the current model — a placeholder plus one option per node — preserving the current selection where it can. It keeps the quick-jump selector in step with the graph as nodes are added or removed.

set_panel_collapsed.name: setPanelCollapsed()
set_panel_collapsed.desc: `setPanelCollapsed(v)` collapses or expands the HUD control panel, toggling the panel body's visibility and the toggle button's state. It is what tucks the panel away to give the galaxy room — called by the toggle directly, and automatically when entering focus.

run_search.name: runSearch()
run_search.desc:
`runSearch()` powers the live search box: it reads the query, matches it against node names, rebuilds the results list, and shows or hides the dropdown. Matching happens as you type, and the results are keyboard-navigable — the current selection is tracked so the arrow keys and Enter work.

It is the entry point of the search subsystem; choosing a result hands off to `pickSearch` to actually travel to the node.

pick_search.name: pickSearch()
pick_search.desc: `pickSearch(id)` commits a choice from the search box: it clears and blurs the query, resolves the node, and navigates to it — entering its system or focusing it as appropriate. It is what turns a search hit into actually going there.
pick_search.code: function pickSearch(id){ qEl.value=""; resultsEl.style.display="none"; qMatches=[]; qSel=-1; qEl.blur(); const _i=Model.index(id); if(_i==null||_i<0) return; if(Focus.mode==="focus" && typeof exitFocus==="function") exitFocus(); if(typeof window!=="undefined" && typeof window.hlClickNode==="function") window.hlClickNode(_i); else goToNode(_i); }

q_highlight.name: qHighlight()
q_highlight.desc: `qHighlight()` updates which search-result row looks selected, toggling the `sel` class so the highlighted entry matches the current keyboard position. It is the small visual half of navigating the results list with the arrow keys.

attach_long_press.name: attachLongPress()
attach_long_press.desc: `attachLongPress(el, fn)` wires a long-press gesture onto an element: a press held still for a moment, without dragging away, fires the callback; any movement or an early release cancels it. It is the shared gesture behind opening the inline editor by holding a card, kept in one place so press-and-hold behaves consistently wherever it is used.

close_editor.name: closeEditor()
close_editor.desc: `closeEditor()` now simply clears the editing target. It survives as a small reset called by navigation — entering a subgraph, climbing the breadcrumb — after the unreachable full-editor panel it used to hide was removed.

types_apply_live.name: typesApplyLive()
types_apply_live.desc: `typesApplyLive()` applies a connector-type change immediately across the app: it rebuilds the legend, the visibility flags and the renderer's colours, and refreshes the focus view. It is what makes editing a type update the galaxy live rather than after a reload.
types_apply_live.code: function typesApplyLive(){ buildLegend(); rebuildVis(); Renderer.refresh(); if(Focus.mode==="focus") refocusCards(); saveRoot(); }

ed_type_card.name: edTypeCard()
ed_type_card.desc: `edTypeCard(k, types, tpList)` builds one editable connector-type card in the types panel: its label or labels, colour, arrow and dashed style, a count of how many links use it, and edit/delete controls. Split out of `renderTypesPanel`'s per-type loop.

render_edit_panel.name: renderEditPanel()
render_edit_panel.desc: `renderEditPanel(listId, items, emptyMsg, cardFn)` renders one of the editing panels — a list element cleared and refilled with one card per item via the supplied `cardFn`, or an empty-state message when there are none. It is the shared body of `renderTypesPanel` (Connectors) and `renderGroupsPanel` (Groups), which differ only in their list, data and card builder.

render_types_panel.name: renderTypesPanel()
render_types_panel.desc: `renderTypesPanel()` renders the Connectors panel — one editable card per connector type, through the shared `renderEditPanel` with `edTypeCard`. It is reachable from the 'Connectors' button in the control panel, and refreshed when a type changes.
render_types_panel.code: function renderTypesPanel(){ renderEditPanel("tp-list", Model.raw.types||{}, "No types yet \u2014 create one when adding a connection", edTypeCard); }

ed_group_card.name: edGroupCard()
ed_group_card.desc: `edGroupCard(k, groups, gpList)` builds one editable group card in the groups panel: the group's label, colour swatch, a count of member nodes, and edit/delete controls. Split out of `renderGroupsPanel`'s per-group loop.

render_groups_panel.name: renderGroupsPanel()
render_groups_panel.desc: `renderGroupsPanel()` renders the Groups panel — one editable card per group, through the shared `renderEditPanel` with `edGroupCard`. It is reachable from the 'Groups' button in the control panel, and refreshed when a group changes.
render_groups_panel.code: function renderGroupsPanel(){ renderEditPanel("gp-list", Model.raw.groups||{}, "No groups yet \u2014 create one from a node\u2019s Group field", edGroupCard); }

slug_key.name: slugKey()
slug_key.desc: `slugKey(base, obj)` generates a unique key from a base string — lowercased and hyphenated — that does not collide with existing keys in `obj`, appending a suffix if needed. Used when creating new groups and connector types so each gets a stable, unique id.
slug_key.code: function slugKey(base, obj){ let s=String(base||"x").toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g,"-").replace(/^-+|-+$/g,"")||"x", k=s, i=2; while(obj[k]) k=s+"-"+(i++); return k; }

type_name.name: typeName()
type_name.desc: `typeName(k)` returns the display label for a connector type `k` — its own label if mutual, or a directional phrasing otherwise. The small helper that turns a type key into readable text wherever a connection's type is shown.
type_name.code: function typeName(k){ const t=(Model.raw.types||{})[k]||{}; return t.mutual ? (t.label||k) : ((t.fromLabel||k)+" \u2192 "+(t.toLabel||k)); }

refocus_cards.name: refocusCards()
refocus_cards.desc: `refocusCards()` re-gathers the focused node's neighbours and rebuilds the card constellation — used after an edit changes what a node connects to, so the focus view immediately reflects the new relationships.

conn_topology_changed.name: connTopologyChanged()
conn_topology_changed.desc: `connTopologyChanged()` is the after-an-edit refresh. When links are added or removed it reloads the model, rebuilds the visibility flags and the renderer's colours, updates the node and edge counts, and re-lays the focus cards — so the galaxy's solar structure reflects the new topology. It is the single call every editing path makes to say 'the connections changed — re-derive everything that depends on them'.

build_link_panel.name: buildLinkPanel()
build_link_panel.desc: `buildLinkPanel(panel, l)` builds the editing panel for a single existing connection — fields for its description and labels — so a link's own text can be edited directly. Used where a connection is inspected in detail rather than just retyped.

sync.name: sync()
sync.desc: `sync()` is a nested status helper in the image-field wiring: it updates the label and remove control to reflect whether an uploaded image is in use versus a URL. A small piece of the editor's image controls.
sync.code: function sync(){ if(isData()){ st.textContent="Uploaded image in use"; rm.style.display=""; ip.style.display="none"; } else { st.textContent=""; rm.style.display=l.img?"":"none"; ip.style.display=""; } }

delete_node_by_id.name: deleteNodeById()
delete_node_by_id.desc: `deleteNodeById(gone)` removes a node and all of its links from the model, snapshotting first so the operation stays coherent. It is the low-level deletion used both by the delete controls and by node-merging.

conn_builder_html.name: connBuilderHtml()
conn_builder_html.desc: `connBuilderHtml()` returns the static markup for the New connection panel: the title, the two node-search fields, the connector-type selector with its inline new-type fields, the add-code button, and the Cancel and Create actions. A pure template that `openConnBuilder` injects and then wires.

open_conn_builder.name: openConnBuilder()
open_conn_builder.desc:
`openConnBuilder()` opens the New connection builder — the panel for creating a link between two nodes. It injects the markup from `connBuilderHtml`, then wires the two node searches, the connector-type selector (including defining a new type inline), the add-code button that attaches a `code` block to the pending link, and the Create action that pushes the finished link into the model.

It is the deliberate way to add a connection between any two nodes, as opposed to the drag-to-connect gesture in the focus view.

loop.name: loop()
loop.desc:
`loop()` is the animation heartbeat. Scheduled every frame, it advances time, eases the camera toward its targets — distance, centre, rotation — so movement glides instead of snapping, advances the planet spin, calls `frame` to draw, and re-schedules itself. Where `frame` renders a single still, `loop` is what makes the galaxy live and move.

It also drives the per-frame housekeeping that is not drawing: keeping the info card in step through `updatePlanetInfo`, refreshing toggle buttons, and handling automatic transitions such as dropping focus when the moment is right. Because it runs continuously it clamps its own timestep, so a single slow frame can not make the camera lurch.

confirm_replace.name: confirmReplace()
confirm_replace.desc: `confirmReplace(proceed)` guards any action that would replace the current graph. If nothing has been edited it simply proceeds; if there are unsaved changes it shows a warning first and only runs the pending action once you confirm. It is the safety net that stops an accidental load from silently discarding your work.
confirm_replace.code: function confirmReplace(proceed){ if(!graphDirty){ proceed(); return; } _pendingReplace=proceed; const w=document.getElementById("examplewarn"); if(w) w.style.display="flex"; else proceed(); }

open_about.name: openAbout()
open_about.desc: `openAbout()` opens the about card — a small overlay describing the app — creating it on first use and toggling it into view. A self-contained piece of chrome, unrelated to the graph itself.

close_launcher.name: closeLauncher()
close_launcher.desc: `closeLauncher()` closes the launcher overlay and removes the `launcher-active` body class, so the CSS restores the controls and the galaxy underneath. The counterpart to `openLauncher`.
close_launcher.code: function closeLauncher(){ const el=document.getElementById("launcher"); if(el) el.style.display="none"; try{ window._launcherOpen=false; document.body.classList.remove("launcher-active"); }catch(_){} }

fetch_graph_manifest.name: fetchGraphManifest()
fetch_graph_manifest.desc: `fetchGraphManifest()` fetches `graphs/manifest.json` and returns the list of available documents, tolerating an absent or malformed manifest by falling back to an empty list. It is what the launcher calls to learn which graphs to offer.

fetch_graph_doc.name: fetchGraphDoc()
fetch_graph_doc.desc: `fetchGraphDoc(url, name)` fetches a single graph document by URL and returns it ready to load, wrapping the response so the rest of the loading path can treat a remote document like an uploaded file. It is the network half of opening a graph from the picker.

open_launcher.name: openLauncher()
open_launcher.desc:
`openLauncher(opts)` opens the launcher — the graph picker reached from the Load button, and shown on first run. It reads the manifest and lists each server-side graph as a two-action row: tap the name to load it, or tap Merge to fold it into the current graph. Alongside the manifest it offers Resume, Open a file… and Merge a file… (client-side), Start a new graph, About, and — when dismissable — Cancel.

It is the single entry point for all loading, server-side and client-side; the separate Example button and the old load dialog have been folded into it.

draw_backdrop.name: drawBackdrop()
draw_backdrop.desc: Draws the fullscreen gradient backdrop quad (dark base plus a radial depth-glow) as the farthest layer.
draw_backdrop.code: function drawBackdrop(dw,dh,cx,cy,rad){ if(!bkProg) return; gl.useProgram(bkProg); gl.bindVertexArray(bkVao); gl.uniform2f(bkUni.viewport,dw,dh); gl.uniform2f(bkUni.center,cx,cy); gl.uniform1f(bkUni.rad,rad); gl.disable(gl.BLEND); gl.drawArrays(gl.TRIANGLE_STRIP,0,4); gl.enable(gl.BLEND); gl.bindVertexArray(null); }

draw_clouds.name: drawClouds()
draw_clouds.desc: Draws the nebula clouds as textured quads, sampling the 5-layer cloud texture-array with a screen blend.
draw_clouds.code: function drawClouds(cc,dw,dh){ if(!clProg||!clTex||cc<=0) return; gl.useProgram(clProg); gl.bindVertexArray(clVao); gl.uniform2f(clUni.viewport,dw,dh); gl.activeTexture(gl.TEXTURE0); gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY, clTex); gl.uniform1i(clUni.tex,0); gl.blendFunc(gl.ONE, gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_COLOR); gl.drawArraysInstanced(gl.TRIANGLE_STRIP,0,4,cc); gl.blendFunc(gl.SRC_ALPHA, gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA); gl.bindVertexArray(null); }

draw_sprites.name: drawSprites()
draw_sprites.desc: Draws soft additive glow points through the sprite program — background stars and drifting dust, and foreground effect glows.
draw_sprites.code: function drawSprites(sc,dw,dh){ if(!sProg||sc<=0) return; gl.useProgram(sProg); gl.bindVertexArray(sVao); gl.uniform2f(sUni.viewport, dw, dh); gl.blendFunc(gl.ONE, gl.ONE); gl.drawArraysInstanced(gl.TRIANGLE_STRIP,0,4,sc); gl.blendFunc(gl.SRC_ALPHA, gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA); gl.bindVertexArray(null); }

draw_connectors.name: drawConnectors()
draw_connectors.desc: Draws the galaxy connector web: one instanced quad per front-facing edge in a single faint colour.
draw_connectors.code: function drawConnectors(cc,dw,dh,col,wd){ if(!lnProg||cc<=0) return; gl.useProgram(lnProg); gl.bindVertexArray(lnVao); gl.uniform2f(lnUni.viewport,dw,dh); gl.uniform1f(lnUni.w,wd); gl.uniform4f(lnUni.col,col[0],col[1],col[2],col[3]); gl.blendFunc(gl.ONE, gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA); gl.drawArraysInstanced(gl.TRIANGLE_STRIP,0,4,cc); gl.blendFunc(gl.SRC_ALPHA, gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA); gl.bindVertexArray(null); }

draw_ef_lines.name: drawEfLines()
draw_ef_lines.desc: Draws effect lines through the effect-line program with additive or over blend — ego spokes, focus constellation, tap-glow, trails, sun starbursts.
draw_ef_lines.code: function drawEfLines(n,dw,dh,fill,over){ if(!efProg||n<=0) return; if(n>efCap){ efCap=Math.max(n,efCap*2,64); efInst=new Float32Array(efCap*EF_STRIDE); } fill(efInst); gl.bindBuffer(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER,efInstBuf); gl.bufferData(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER,efInst.subarray(0,n*EF_STRIDE),gl.DYNAMIC_DRAW); gl.useProgram(efProg); gl.bindVertexArray(efVao); gl.uniform2f(efUni.viewport,dw,dh); gl.blendFunc(gl.ONE, over?gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA:gl.ONE); gl.drawArraysInstanced(gl.TRIANGLE_STRIP,0,4,n); gl.blendFunc(gl.SRC_ALPHA,gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA); gl.bindVertexArray(null); }

draw_fg_glows.name: drawFgGlows()
draw_fg_glows.desc: Draws foreground glow sprites layered over the bodies (tap ripples, ignition flare, sun coronas that sit in front).
draw_fg_glows.code: function drawFgGlows(n,dw,dh,fill){ if(!sProg||!fgVao||n<=0) return; if(n>fgCap){ fgCap=Math.max(n,fgCap*2,64); fgInst=new Float32Array(fgCap*S_STRIDE); } fill(fgInst); gl.bindBuffer(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER,fgInstBuf); gl.bufferData(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER,fgInst.subarray(0,n*S_STRIDE),gl.DYNAMIC_DRAW); gl.useProgram(sProg); gl.bindVertexArray(fgVao); gl.uniform2f(sUni.viewport,dw,dh); gl.blendFunc(gl.ONE,gl.ONE); gl.drawArraysInstanced(gl.TRIANGLE_STRIP,0,4,n); gl.blendFunc(gl.SRC_ALPHA,gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA); gl.bindVertexArray(null); }

draw_overlay.name: drawOverlay()
draw_overlay.desc: Post-render screen pass that draws the focus-card constellation lines and chevron arrowheads over the finished scene.
draw_overlay.code: function drawOverlay(dw,dh,n,fill){ if(!ok||!efProg||n<=0) return; gl.bindFramebuffer(gl.FRAMEBUFFER,null); gl.viewport(0,0,dw,dh); gl.enable(gl.BLEND); drawEfLines(n,dw,dh,fill,true); }

upload_clouds.name: uploadClouds()
upload_clouds.desc: Builds the cloud texture-array once from the makeCloudSprite images, so drawClouds can sample all five layers in one pass.
upload_clouds.code: function uploadClouds(cvns){ if(!ok||!clProg||!cvns||!cvns.length) return; try{ clTex=gl.createTexture(); gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY, clTex); const S=cvns[0].width||256, N=cvns.length; gl.texImage3D(gl.TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY,0,gl.RGBA,S,S,N,0,gl.RGBA,gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE,null); gl.pixelStorei(gl.UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL,true); for(let i=0;i<N;i++) gl.texSubImage3D(gl.TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY,0,0,0,i,S,S,1,gl.RGBA,gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE,cvns[i]); gl.pixelStorei(gl.UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL,false); gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY,gl.TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER,gl.LINEAR); gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY,gl.TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER,gl.LINEAR); gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY,gl.TEXTURE_WRAP_S,gl.CLAMP_TO_EDGE); gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY,gl.TEXTURE_WRAP_T,gl.CLAMP_TO_EDGE); clN=N; }catch(_){ clTex=null; } }

wormhole.name: wormholes & the journey
wormhole.desc:
A node or link carrying a `subgraph` is reached through a **wormhole** — an animated portal you fly *into*, plunging through a hyperspace tunnel to arrive in the nested graph. Three kinds: a **sun portal** on a hub node with its own subgraph; a **connection portal** floating above a planet joined to the focused node by a subgraph-bearing link; and a **return portal** below the connecting node inside any subgraph that flies you back out.

Where `enterSubgraph` is the plain graph-stack descent, the wormhole is the felt version: collect the portals every frame, tap the bubble or its label, fly the camera into it, cover the switch with a tunnel, load the destination behind that cover, then iris it open. The pieces below make that happen.

portal_collect.name: portal collection (per frame)
portal_collect.desc: Every frame the renderer rebuilds two arrays: `_PORTALS` (a flat draw buffer — screen centre, two foreshortening axes, depth and colour, ten floats per portal) and `_PORTALHIT` (one record per portal with the bubble circle `x,y,r`, the real 3-D position `px3/py3/pz3` and radius `pr3`, the label rect `lx/ly/lw/lh`, and the group colour). Two loops feed them: a standalone loop over every subgraph-bearing sun, **decoupled from visibility** so a sun portal never drops out as its star scrolls off; and a connection loop over the focused node's subgraph links that skips off-screen nodes **except the one currently being flown into**. Each pushes the sun→portal connector too. `_PORTALS` is then drawn depth-interleaved with the planets, and *regardless of body count*, so a portal never vanishes on close approach.

portal_warp.name: portalWarp()
portal_warp.desc: `portalWarp(i, subDoc, entryId)` runs a forward journey. It hides the connectors, snapshots the view, resolves the destination group colour from the hit record, and creates the `_warp` state object with `loaded:false`. It aims the camera at the portal's stored 3-D position (`px3/py3/pz3`) with a tiny target distance, so the camera flies *into* the bubble rather than at the planet beneath it. On timers it loads the subgraph at **+1200ms** (behind the tunnel cover), fires a decoupled reveal at **+2000ms** — snapping the look-at to target and blasting — and keeps an **+8000ms** safety fallback. A `_warpSeq` id on the object and every timer stops a stale journey's timer from acting on a newer one.

exit_portal.name: exitPortal()
exit_portal.desc: `exitPortal()` is the return journey, mirrored on `portalWarp`. It finds the node matching `Focus._returnNode`, flies into *its* return portal exactly as the forward trip flies into a wormhole, and copies its colour. On the same +1200ms / +2000ms / +8000ms timers it loads the parent through `exitToLevel` and reveals. If no return portal can be found it falls back to a plain zoom-out.
exit_portal.code: function exitPortal(){ if(!graphStack.length) return; view.showConnectors=false; _warp={t0:performance.now(), blastAt:null, loaded:false, col:[0.55,0.65,1.0], id:(++_warpSeq)}; var _wid=_warp.id; var _flew=false; try{ if(Focus._returnNode!=null){ let _ri=-1; for(let k=0;k<Model.ids.length;k++){ if(Model.ids[k]===Focus._returnNode){ _ri=k; break; } } if(_ri>=0 && SolarSys.disp && SolarSys.disp[_ri]){ const _dp=SolarSys.disp[_ri]; const _sr2=(SolarSys.sunR&&SolarSys.sunR[_ri])||((SolarSys.Rmax||40)*0.6); view.tcx=_dp.x; view.tcy=_dp.y+_sr2*5.3; view.tcz=_dp.z; view.tdist=Math.max(0.15,_sr2*0.06); view.flyTarget=-1; _warp.nodeIdx=_ri; try{ const _phc=_PORTALHIT&&_PORTALHIT.find(p=>p&&p.node===_ri&&p.col); if(_phc) _warp.col=_phc.col; }catch(_){} try{ const _ph2=_PORTALHIT&&_PORTALHIT.find(p=>p&&p.node===_ri); _warp.px=_ph2?_ph2.x/innerWidth:0.5; _warp.py=_ph2?(1.0-_ph2.y/innerHeight):0.5; }catch(_dv){} _flew=true; } } }catch(_fv){} if(!_flew){ view.tdist=Math.max(view.dist*3.5, 60); } if(_warp.px==null){ _warp.px=0.5; _warp.py=0.5; } setTimeout(()=>{ if(_warp && _warp.id===_wid){ _warp.loaded=true; exitToLevel(graphStack.length-1); view.showConnectors=true; } }, 1200); setTimeout(()=>{ if(_warp && _warp.id===_wid && _warp.blastAt==null){ try{ view.cx=view.tcx; view.cy=view.tcy; view.cz=view.tcz; Focus._igTargetScreenR=0; }catch(_zf){} _warp.blastAt=performance.now(); } }, 2000); setTimeout(()=>{ if(_warp && _warp.id===_wid && _warp.blastAt==null) _warp.blastAt=performance.now(); }, 8000); }

enter_subgraph_doc.name: enterSubgraphDoc()
enter_subgraph_doc.desc: `enterSubgraphDoc(doc, focusId, savedView, entryId)` is the load half of a wormhole trip, called by `portalWarp` mid-flight (not by a tap). It pushes the parent onto `graphStack` — recording its title, saved view, focus id and return node — then **transiently overrides the child's `start` with the parent's entry node** so the nested layout seeds and focuses on that node, loads the child, restores `start`, and egos onto the entry. The transient override is why the same subgraph reached from different parents each opens on its own entry.

draw_portal.name: drawPortal() — PORTAL_FS
draw_portal.desc: `drawPortal(...)` renders one wormhole through the `PORTAL_FS` fragment shader: a screen-aligned **glass bubble** (round from every camera angle) lensing a procedural destination galaxy, wrapped by an Interstellar-style **accretion vortex** and photon ring on a foreshortening disc, all mixed toward the group colour. It draws *inside the scene framebuffer*, depth-interleaved with the planets so bodies occlude and are occluded correctly. The two elliptical axes it takes give the disc its foreshortening; they are clamped when they blow up near the camera plane.
draw_portal.code: function drawPortal(cx,cy,aax,aay,abx,aby,pdepth,cr,cg,cb,time,dw,dh){ if(!pPortal||!fsqVao) return; gl.useProgram(pPortal); gl.bindVertexArray(fsqVao); gl.uniform2f(pUni.res,dw,dh); gl.uniform2f(pUni.center,cx,cy); gl.uniform2f(pUni.axisA,aax,aay); gl.uniform2f(pUni.axisB,abx,aby); gl.uniform1f(pUni.time,time); gl.uniform3f(pUni.color,cr,cg,cb); gl.disable(gl.DEPTH_TEST); gl.depthMask(false); gl.enable(gl.BLEND); gl.blendFunc(gl.ONE,gl.ONE); gl.drawArrays(gl.TRIANGLE_STRIP,0,4); gl.blendFunc(gl.SRC_ALPHA,gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA); }

draw_tunnel.name: drawTunnel() — TUNNEL_FS
draw_tunnel.desc: `drawTunnel(...)` renders the hyperspace tunnel full-screen while a journey is in flight (only when `_warp` is set). Its `TUNNEL_FS` shader layers four sets of **discrete streaking stars** — each a bright head with a motion-blur tail rushing outward with perspective and a soft glow halo — over a drifting **nebular haze**, with a **Doppler** cool-centre / warm-rim grade and a breathing **barrel-lens** distortion, all in the destination group colour with white-hot cores. It **irises open from the throat** rather than hard-cutting, and the destination punches through the centre as the reveal phase climbs.
draw_tunnel.code: function drawTunnel(t,phase,cr,cg,cb,dw,dh){ if(!pTunnel||!fsqVao) return; gl.useProgram(pTunnel); gl.bindVertexArray(fsqVao); gl.uniform2f(ptU.res,dw,dh); gl.uniform1f(ptU.time,t); gl.uniform1f(ptU.phase,phase); gl.uniform3f(ptU.color,cr,cg,cb); gl.disable(gl.DEPTH_TEST); gl.enable(gl.BLEND); gl.blendFunc(gl.SRC_ALPHA,gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA); gl.drawArrays(gl.TRIANGLE_STRIP,0,4); }

links.details: `load` never touches raw JSON directly. It hands the incoming document to `normalize`, which applies defaults and builds the slug list, index map and adjacency tables, and only stores the result once that indexed structure comes back. This edge is the boundary between a *raw document* and the *working model*.
the startup load path folds the first document into the model through `Model.load`.
the top-level load path normalises the raw document into the working model through `normalize`.
the initial colour setup resolves node colours through `colorName`.
transient status messages appear via `showInfoCard`.
a file upload is parsed into a document via `parseJsonOrZip`.
boot kicks off the force-layout settling through `run` once the first document is loaded.
before the first layout, the load path seeds node positions via `seedInto`.
boot stands up PlanetGL's WebGL2 renderer through its `init` during startup.
`render`, PlanetGL's GPU draw, is part of the render path the boot code stands up.
`labelTex` caches label textures for that render path.
`drawLabels` belongs to the label render path the boot code initialises.
boot calls `resize` at startup and on every window-resize event to fit the canvas to the viewport.
boot refreshes the renderer's colour indices via `Renderer.refresh` once a document is loaded.
`frame`, the per-frame renderer, is referenced from the top-level render bootstrap that the loop drives.
boot wires `pick`, the canvas hit-test, into the pointer handlers, so tapping the galaxy selects a body.
the pointer handlers use `pickConnector` to detect taps on a connector inside the focused system.
and `pickAnyConnector` to detect taps on any connector across the whole galaxy.
the camera/pointer code reads the focused system's on-screen diameter via `centerDia`.
and its on-screen position via `centerScreen`.
and clear the relations panel via `hideRelInfo`.

`seedInto` spreads nodes from a reproducible arrangement rather than random noise, drawing each starting coordinate from `seededUnit`, whose value is fixed by the graph's seed. That dependency is what makes a given document settle into the same layout every time.

Before the first simulation step, `run` calls `seedInto` to give every node a starting position — the force solver only refines an existing arrangement, so without a seed it would have nothing to relax. Seeding deterministically also keeps successive runs stable.

`run` is the streaming layout path; when the incremental route isn't usable it falls back to `runSync`, which settles the same simulation in one blocking pass. The edge marks a graceful degradation from progressive to synchronous layout, not two different algorithms.
`sizeFB` allocates each offscreen target's storage with `tex`, which creates the empty RGBA texture the framebuffer will render into.
It then wraps each of those textures in a framebuffer via `fbo`, giving the glow and blur passes somewhere to draw off-screen.
PlanetGL's `init` compiles its shaders through `sh` — GLSL source becomes a compiled shader object, or null on a compile error.
It sets up the text-label pipeline via `initLabels` as part of GPU initialisation.
Every frame `render` calls `sizeFB` to make sure the offscreen targets still match the viewport before it draws into them.
Once the targets and uniforms are ready, `render` issues the actual instanced sphere draw through `drawPlanets`.
`link2` compiles its two shaders with `sh` before linking; if either compile fails, `sh` returns null and `link2` abandons the program.
`initLabels` builds its dedicated label shader program with `link2`.
`buildGalaxy` scatters dust clouds produced by `makeCloudSprite` to give the backdrop its nebular texture.
It bakes the tileable star texture via `buildStars`.
It bakes the whole galaxy backdrop — stars, glow, clouds — via `buildGalaxy`.
Finally it sizes the canvas and backdrop to the window with `resize`.
`frame` calls `ensure` first each tick so the projection buffers are sized for the current node count before anything writes into them.
`frame()` calls `buildSolarTopology()`.
`frame()` calls `buildSolarOrbits()`.
`frame()` calls `clamp()`.
`frame()` calls `galaxyPosNow()`.
`frame()` calls `degFactor()`.

`frame()` calls `toEdge()`.

`pickConnector` measures how near a tap falls to each connector in the focused system; the actual point-to-line distance is computed by `segDist`, so the picker only has to compare the numbers it returns.
Same geometry, wider net — `pickAnyConnector` uses `segDist` to gauge a tap's distance to every edge in the galaxy, not just the focused system's.
`flyOut` needs a target distance that frames the whole galaxy; `universeFitDist` supplies it, and `flyOut` then eases the camera toward it. One decides *how far back*, the other *goes there*.
`isVisible` asks `groupOf` which group a node belongs to, then checks whether that group is currently hidden.
`rebuildVis` runs `isVisible` for every node to bake the fast per-index visibility flags the frame path reads.

`toggleGroup()` calls `exitFocus()`.

`videoBlock()` calls `esc()`.
It builds the embeddable URL from a YouTube link through `ytEmbed`.

`index.html` is the whole engine, so it is the principal part of the project — the single file you deploy and open. Everything else the project ships exists to feed it.
The manifest belongs to the project's data side: it's the index the launcher reads to know which graph documents exist. It's part of Xanadu, but content-facing rather than code.
The HTML shell is literally the `<body>` of `index.html` — the static markup the script mounts into. It isn't a separate file; it's a region of the engine file.
The floating controls and HUD are declared as static markup inside `index.html`'s body; the script only toggles and populates them.
The structured editor's markup lives in `index.html`; the script fills its fields but doesn't create the panel.
The overlay containers are part of `index.html`'s body — though a few (the launcher, the code lightbox) are created by script at runtime rather than declared up front.
The design tokens live in the `<style>` block of `index.html`; there is no separate stylesheet to load.
The component classes are defined in `index.html`'s `<style>` block, alongside the tokens they build on.
The state/mode rules are part of `index.html`'s CSS — the same stylesheet, a distinct job.

The manifest is a directory of the graph documents: each entry names a file in `graphs/` and its title, and the launcher loads whichever the reader picks. The manifest knows *of* the documents; it doesn't contain them.

At its core the engine is a reader of graph documents: it loads a JSON of nodes, links, groups and types and renders it. Everything else — layout, cards, editing, export — operates on whatever document is loaded.
